searchText: "Rough consensus and running code." Unlike the blockchain, human consensus doesn't have to be 100%. It's best when it is, but most people can go along with decisions they disagree with when necessary. What's really bad is when a developer or team is so much in disagreement they would prefer to leave. Everyone would need to be very sure of their position to let that happen. So far it hasn't. <@!552133098075193354> > long term cost of running a node (w/o massive DB improvements) How massive? So as I know nobody is using DBs designed to purpose - they are tweaking general-purpose DBs to more-or-less do the job. <@!683653554631868440> I meant erigon-style flat DB architecture, not improvements to actual DB providers Yes. I meant actually designing the DB code to best fit the architecture.

excerpts.content: "Rough consensus and running code."  Unlike the blockchain, human consensus doesn't have to be 100%.  It's best when it is, but most people can go along with decisions they disagree with when necessary.  What's really bad is when a developer or team is so much in disagreement they would prefer to leave.  Everyone would need to be very sure of their position to let that happen.  So far it hasn't.

excerpts.author: gcolvin
excerpts.content:
<@!552133098075193354>
> long term cost of running a node (w/o massive DB improvements) 
How massive?  So as I know nobody is using DBs designed to purpose - they are tweaking general-purpose DBs to more-or-less do the job.

excerpts.content: <@!683653554631868440> I meant erigon-style flat DB architecture, not improvements to actual DB providers

excerpts.content: Yes.  I meant actually designing the DB code to best fit the architecture.
